title: Fix ReplanGovernor graduated backoff off-by-one (F9/F11)
description:
## Finding F9/F11 (Council: P1, 90% confidence)

ReplanGovernor implements a graduated backoff schedule [5, 10, 20, 30] seconds for stall recovery delays. Two bugs:

1. **Off-by-one**: _stallAttempt is incremented from 0→1 in the same call that declares the stall. When CurrentStallDelay reads `_graduatedDelaysSec[Math.Min(_stallAttempt, 3)]`, it gets index 1 = 10s instead of index 0 = 5s. The first stall always waits 10s, not 5s.

2. **Auto-recovery resets counter**: Auto-recovery (both inline in Evaluate and in TryAutoRecover) resets _stallAttempt to 0, same as RecordProgress. Since the same underlying problem usually persists, the next stall starts from 0→1 again, getting 10s again. Tiers 3 and 4 (20s, 30s) and tier 1 (5s) are unreachable in normal operation.

## Why not caught
ReplanGovernorTests.cs uses a single-element delay array [0], which makes the off-by-one invisible since Math.Min(_stallAttempt, 0) is always 0 regardless of _stallAttempt's value.

## Recommendation
1. Only RecordProgress/Reset should clear _stallAttempt. Auto-recovery should leave it untouched so backoff escalates: 5→10→20→30→30...
2. Fix off-by-one: compute delay index from _stallAttempt - 1 (clamped at 0) at the point the stall is declared, or read the delay before incrementing
3. Add a test with the real [5, 10, 20, 30] array asserting the first stall's CurrentStallDelay is 5s
